title: 1966 AHSME Problem 28
statement: Five points \(O,\) \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D\) are taken in order on a straight line with distances \(OA=a,\) \(OB=b,\) \(OC=c,\) and \(OD=d.\) \(P\) is a point on the line between \(B\) and \(C\) and such that \(AP:PD=BP:PC.\) Then \(OP\) equals:

solutions.text:
Let \(p=OP.\) The given ratio becomes \[ \frac{p-a}{d-p}=\frac{p-b}{c-p}. \] Cross-multiplication cancels the \(p^2\) terms and yields \[ p(a-b+c-d)=ac-bd. \] Therefore \(p=\frac{ac-bd}{a-b+c-d}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Cross-multiply the two given ratios after making those substitutions
